notes: Inbound SMB lead — small healthtech app that routes patient support to internal ticketing system.
Primary ask: use Hosted API (self-serve) to build a streaming support-agent. They want model to emit structured JSON for tickets and call a tool to create tickets in their system.

Symptoms reported: when streaming JSON mode is enabled the app receives multiple partial chunks that are not valid JSON until stream end. Their client-side parser throws and drops the response. Example attached in INF-2143.

Function calling issues: model occasionally emits arguments that don't match function schema (e.g., ticket_id as number vs string; missing required 'priority' field). They pass a function schema and expect strict conformance.
Customer quote: "We need a predictable JSON object per response so we can call our createTicket endpoint reliably" — lead engineer on call.
Workarounds tried by customer: buffering stream until 'DONE' sentinel (fragile), switching off streaming (latency bad), adding post-hoc JSON repair heuristics (flaky).

Root-cause hypotheses from SE: (1) streaming tokenization can split JSON tokens across chunks; (2) model generation sometimes includes extra commentary around JSON; (3) older client SDK strips metadata that would help reassembly; (4) function schema enforcement is probabilistic unless using our function_call strict mode or a canonical wrapper prompt.

SE notes: need minimal reproducible case with exact prompt, model variant, SDK version. Recommend trying function_call mode (functions list + function_call: "auto") or using our structured-output JSON-mode best-practice: wrap JSON in fenced codeblock, include output schema in system msg, and add explicit final token like "__END_JSON__" to make streaming assembly simpler.
Customer constraints: committed to public cloud hosted_api (no VPC). Wants minimal code changes. Cost sensitive — will prefer lower token churn. Will evaluate final approach during 2-week POC.

Ask from AE/SE: provide a patched SDK snippet for streaming-safe JSON assembly (server-side), sample prompt patterns and function schema examples. Also request recommended model variants that are most stable for strict function outputs.
Stated timeline: aiming for a light POC by end of April; procurement if POC meets reliability and cost targets.
